text: Keystone is a reference skill plus a review command and a reviewer agent, with no hooks.
author: claude-code
rationale: The reference loads on demand when an agent designs; a hook would add context to ordinary coding sessions that do not need it.
cost_if_wrong: A hook added later would change when guidance appears; the skill trigger text would need rework.
choice: skills/architecture (reference, model-invoked), skills/architecture-review (user-invoked command), agents/architecture-reviewer; no hooks
alternatives: add a session or prompt hook that injects architecture guidance

text: The review reads design material and a docket ledger when one is present, and does not review code.
author: claude-code
rationale: Architecture lives in decisions and design documents; code review is a separate tool with a different cost profile.
choice: Inputs: given paths, or README, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, docs/, ADR folders, proposals/, design/, specs, plus current docket decisions, claims and open questions; superseded records only for history
alternatives: review source code against the principles

text: Reference content covers the seed research, the gap topics and the broader canon, kept light by one reference file per topic loaded on demand.
author: claude-code
rationale: An agent opens only the topic it needs, so breadth does not cost context.
choice: One file per topic under skills/architecture/references; SKILL.md maps them and says when to open each

text: The reviewer agent defaults to Fable at xhigh effort.
author: claude-code
revisit: A cheaper model produces reviews of the same quality on the same inputs
choice: agents/architecture-reviewer.md frontmatter model: fable, effort: xhigh
